question: What Windows installer TLS recovery policy should OpenClaw ship when npm fails with leaf-certificate verification errors during install.ps1?
rationale: The bug blocks first-time Windows setup, but the obvious retry with --strict-ssl=false changes a package-install trust boundary and needs explicit maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Security-reviewed CA remediation
options.body: Detect the TLS failure and guide or apply explicit cafile/NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS remediation without automatically bypassing certificate verification.

options.title: Operator-approved strict-ssl fallback
options.body: Allow a clearly warned interactive-only --strict-ssl=false retry and fail non-interactive installs with remediation instructions.

options.title: Document external workaround only
options.body: Keep the installer fail-closed and document npm cafile, Windows Hub, or WSL2 alternatives, accepting that this first-run path remains blocked for affected users.

recommendation.title: Security-reviewed CA remediation
recommendation.body: Detect the TLS failure and guide or apply explicit cafile/NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS remediation without automatically bypassing certificate verification.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the densest recent history on Windows installer behavior and install.ps1 failure handling.
